name: Synthetic-diploid benchmark (PacBio-derived)
description:
Constructed from the consensus of multiple variant callers based on short-read data, existing benchmark datasets for evaluating variant calling accuracy are biased toward easy regions accessible by known algorithms. We derived a new benchmark dataset from the
                  de novo
                  PacBio assemblies of two human cell lines that are homozygous across the whole genome. This benchmark provides a more accurate and less biased estimate of the error rate of small variant calls in a realistic context.
evaluation_method: precision / recall / F1 for small variant (SNP/indel) calls against the benchmark truth set
typical_sota_score: ≈99% (high; often in the high-90s for SNPs, lower for difficult indels)
reputation: Well-regarded in the genomics and variant-calling community as a more challenging, less-biased benchmark derived from long-read (PacBio) assemblies to evaluate small-variant accuracy.
notes: Non-ML (bioinformatics) benchmark derived from long-read assemblies; intended to reduce bias present in short-read consensus benchmarks. May still contain assembly or representation artefacts; dataset is specialized and smaller than some population-scale resources.
